title: Northbeam TechWorks Labour Rebilled as Chargeable Work
content:
Work on a Northbeam TechWorks Installation and Repair job is sometimes carried out as plan work and only afterwards refused by the plan's own decision. Where a plan's decision refuses a claim after the work was carried out as plan work, the labour of that line is rebilled to the customer as chargeable work.

The rebill stands on the job as a labour entry of its own, carrying the chargeable hours and the rate they were charged at, and raises the service charges outstanding on the job by the amount billed. The customer's statement of the job then shows that labour, the hours behind it and the rate they were charged at.

## Booking the rebill

The desk books it with the agent-side tool `bill_uncovered_device_labour_51108cc0`, which is unlocked and then called by the agent. It is not among the ordinary desk tools and is reached only once unlocked. One call books one labour entry on that job for that attendance, dated the day it is booked.

## The seven values the call carries

- `service_agreement_id` — an identifier: the reference number of the TechWorks work order or care agreement the labour was carried out under, read from the work orders held on the customer's profile before the call.
- `customer_id` — an identifier: the reference number of the customer profile being billed, read from that profile before the call.
- `work_order_line_reference` — an identifier: the reference number of the single line of work the labour is billed on, read from the entries already booked on that job before the call.
- `visit_date` — the day the attendance the labour was carried out on took place, as YYYY-MM-DD, in the retailer's own local calendar; never left empty.
- `labour_hours` — the chargeable labour recorded on the entry, in hours to one decimal place, rounded half up at that one decimal place before it is passed.
- `hourly_rate` — the rate the labour on this entry is charged at, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed.
- `labour_amount` — the labour to bill, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed, always positive.

## What the call returns

A one-line confirmation string naming the labour entry reference that was created, the job it was booked on, the attendance day, the chargeable hours to one decimal place, the rate in USD to two decimal places, the amount billed in USD to two decimal places and the job's new outstanding service charges in USD to two decimal places. The presence of that entry reference in the reply is what shows the labour was billed.

On success the job carries one more charge and a higher outstanding figure, and the customer can be told what the labour on that attendance comes to.

## Points of judgement on the entry

**The hours, the rate and the amount are three separate values on the entry.** Each is carried in its own right, and the entry keeps all three on file.

**The attendance day and the day of booking are different things.** The day carried on the entry as the attendance day is the day the work was carried out; the entry itself is dated the day it is booked.
